title: USMNT Stock Up, Stock Down: Ellis Snatches Pepi’s Place in November Roster
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:30 PM ESTRicardo Pepi (right) will at home on the couch. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images (Ellis); Maja Hitij/FIFA/Getty Images (Pepi)The U.S. men’s national team will regroup in the coming days for the November international window, eager to capitalize on the thrills of last month when the team ran away with four straight victories to ignite the post-World Cup era with perfection.

Manager Mauricio Pochettino called up 25 men to continue the charge, staring down a two-leg series with Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals that has a berth in the 2027 Gold Cup firmly on the table.

Wednesday’s roster selection spoke volumes to Pochettino’s ambitions for the team. While he returned to many seasoned veterans, the Argentine boss still included his fair share of young, budding talents. No matter how much success his former crop of players found, he knows the future of the team is infinitely brighter.

Pochettino has entrusted certain youngsters over others, while leaving several USMNT stalwarts at home on the couch. It’s the dawn of a new era, and Pochettino hasn’t been afraid to make the tough decisions.
Here is Sports Illustrated’s weekly stock up, stock down analysis for USMNT players.

Mathis Albert could earn big minutes this month. / Julius Frick/picture alliance/Getty ImagesMathis Albert will be feeling grateful for Pochettino’s open mind.

Similar to the strong confidence that the Argentine has in fellow USMNT midfielder Gio Reyna, Pochettino sees something uniquely special in Albert, even if the 17-year-old is playing hardly any minutes at the domestic level.

Pochettino named Reyna to his 2026 World Cup even after the 23-year-old spent much of the 2025–26 season riding Borussia Mönchengladbach’s bench, starting just four matches in the Bundesliga. It didn’t matter to Pochettino because Reyna simply possessed this indiscernible gift, even if no one else could understand it at the time. Pochettino hailed him as “a very special talent,” and Reyna rewarded him with a highlight-reel worthy trivela goal in the World Cup opener and is now enjoying the most successful stint of his career playing for Ligue 1 side Strasbourg. He’s a regular starter for the USMNT now, too.

Likewise, Albert has featured in just two matches for club side Borussia Dortmund over the past three months of the new European season. He actually racked up more minutes playing in his debut camp for the USMNT last month (111 total) than he has across all 12 of the competitive Dortmund fixtures he’s been available for (110).

That reality hasn’t deterred Pochettino, who is adamant to continue feeding Albert minutes and called the teenager up to a second-consecutive senior camp. “He’s a player with a quality that isn’t easy to find,” Pochettino gushed after his roster announcement. “He’s one of the U.S.’s most talented players, and even if he isn’t playing too much at Dortmund, if he’s fully fit, he’s capable of bringing something different to the national team.

“We are convinced that giving him the opportunity to be with us will help him recover his confidence and have the possibility to play more in the future. He’s young, and he’s going to be one of the important players for our future, and it’s the moment to trust and believe in him.”
All eyes will be on Albert to see if he can match the high expectations Pochettino has set for him in the same way Reyna has.

Justin Ellis will return to the USMNT next week. / Grant Halverson/MLS/Getty ImagesA look of relief, rather than excitement, took over Justin Ellis’s face when he scored in the 29th minute  against Canada last month.

It was in that moment the 19-year-old knew he may have secured himself another USMNT call-up. The goal was pivotal. Not only was it the game-winner in the finale of the September-October international window, sealing the Stars and Stripes’ perfect camp, but it encapsulated everything that Pochettino had been begging for.

Less than 10 minutes prior, the young striker had fallen to the turf, clutching his leg and no doubt in agonizing pain. He had suffered an ankle injury as a result of a swift kick to the leg from Canadian midfielder Stephen Eustaquio.

After medical assistance, Ellis was able to stand up by himself and move, but not without an intense limp. Nevertheless, he refused to leave the pitch. He was on a mission to find the back of the net, no matter how much it hurt.

“I’m thinking to myself, ‘I don’t know if I can continue. This is crazy,’” Ellis tells Sports Illustrated. “Then I can hear Pochettino screaming my name like 10 times ... You know what he’s going to ask you: ‘Are you good?’ I do not want to look at him and answer that question.
